analysis.name: Ahmed Alif
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My favorite class that I have taken in this program thusfar. It is clear that he truly cares about his students and our growth. I liked his incorporation of media, and found class discussions to be very interesting and practically applicable.

The syllabus changed many times with up to five readings and two unrelated podcasts a week. Instructions for assignments were unclear, which made scores not consistent. Assignments were returned late, so they could not be applied for future work. Instead of explaining core concepts and frameworks, we were told to google them.

Prof. Alif is radically honest. He makes it clear what you need to do to improve. He's very data and research-oriented, using real frameworks and pushes you to apply them. He's also very responsive, and is flexible when life happens. The syllabus had some early revisions that were a bit confusing, but he addressed it and improved it.

Professor Alif reminded me why I came back to academia in the first place: to challenge wicked problems in a way that still centers, honors, and respects those who are disproportionately harmed by them. They are a rising tide who lifts every boat. If you're lucky enough to take a class, just make some flashcards (they'll help w/ acronyms).

Alif is a kind and attentive professor who listens thoughtfully to students while setting clear expectations early in the semester. His integration of media and podcasts with contemporary issues is especially helpful. If anything, the only weakness is that he listens to his students too much.

review_highlights.comment: Professor Zweig is incredibly intelligent. His lectures are incredible and he does his best to present information in a fair and balanced manner. Be sure to attend his lectures because this is where most of the learning will take place. The history of Israel and Palestine is complicated but the assigned readings really help to fill in the gaps.

Zweig is a cute old man with a lot of experience in what he's talking about - he's been a part of Israeli politics firsthand and he has a funny anecdote or two to share. His lectures are great and very in-depth - if you love history you'll love him. Sometimes he jumps around but if you are typing your notes it's not a problem.

The best thing about him was definitely his vast knowledge of the topics of discussion. You could tell from the get-go that this man is a significant source of information on everything covered in the curriculum. However, the lectures are extremely boring and difficult to follow if you don't keep up with the readings.

Took Zweig for Modern Israel and absolutely loved it. Even though I'm not Jewish, I found the course incredibly relevant and manageable. His lectures are well-structured and interesting. He does a great job teaching multiple perspectives on the controversial history. He also offers lots of extra credit opportunity!

He definitely knows what he's talking about, however his lectures often linger on without engaging the students in discussion. He is clear when it comes to assignements and a fair grader, and overall a great guy but when it comes to lectures make sure you drink some caffeine before you attend.
